reverse_dcf_check: 10.8x NTM EPS (about a 9% earnings yield) with ~$1.1B of FCF-ish EBITDA less capex implies the market only needs low-single-digit growth after FY2029 and ~12-13% comms / ~20% BS margins held; it does not require the FTTH cycle to re-accelerate, which is why the downside is carried by the scenarios rather than the multiple.

sbc_treatment.note: SBC (0.5% of revenue) is deducted inside segment EBIT; EPS excludes only acquired-intangible amortization (as DY and the peers report). Shares fall 1.5%/yr net of buybacks and SBC dilution.

reasoning: Skeptic lane. The print beat (Q3 revenue $2.06B, adj EPS $5.23 vs Zacks $4.56) but the stock fell ~19% because the CEO guided FTTH, the largest driver, down in FY28 and Comms to only mid-single-digit growth; two customers defaulted ($22.7M reserve, excluded from adjusted EPS); operating cash flow was $14.1M with DSO 112 days; and the 10-Q shows supplier-finance obligations up to $524M from $367M a quarter earlier, which flatters cash flow (we take it as debt). Leverage is ~2.3x on $2.84B notional debt (Ba2 CFR). We build Comms +3% in FY28 (below the guide's mid-single digit; the backlog-conversion read of +8% is the upside variant), Comms margin ~12%, Building Systems +18% capped by union electrician supply rather than AI capex demand, margins drifting to 21%. FY28 EPS ~$19 (~5% below the pre-print $20.11), FY29 ~$22.6. Weighing honestly: the stock already prices much of this at 10x forward EPS (vs 14.4x peers), the 2023 fiber-visibility downgrade (B. Riley) was followed by continued growth, insiders bought on the way down, and the company is buying stock. Exit P/E 10.8x (k=0.8 shrink) gives a $219 base; the downside (P10 $115) assumes deeper FTTH cuts, ~10.5% comms margin, more credit losses and ~8x; the upside (P90 $344) needs backlog conversion and a re-rate toward the peers. Left tail is fatter than the right. Research limited: SEC documents and the Q3 release could not be fetched directly (blocked), so figures come from XBRL tags, the transcript and press summaries of the slides.

model_inputs.structure_note: Annual driver set (4 drivers: comms revenue, BS revenue, two segment adj EBITDA margins) mapped into a two-segment build; EBIT = segment adj EBITDA less depreciation, less SBC (0.5% of revenue, allocated to both segments), so EPS is on the adjusted, ex-amortization basis that DY and the peers report, with SBC costed. Value carried by P/E (0.75) on the build's NTM EPS at the horizon, EV/EBITDA (0.25) as mid-cycle cross-check; no DCF. Supplier-finance obligations taken as debt via an adjustment.
model_inputs.gap_note: Not quarterly (forecaster set). FTTH/long-haul split is not disclosed, so comms is driven at segment level with components argued in text. Consensus feeds were still pre-print on 2026-11-25 (Zacks FY28 EPS 20.11, revenue 8.52B); post-print revisions will likely move them down toward our build. Non-operating 'other' (~-10M/yr, F86) not carried separately; it is ~$0.25/share. Peer table prices (peers.md) are older than 2026-11-24 closes; repriced median used.

track_record.note: FY26 first guide was 10-13% growth on FY25 4,702.0 (F2) = 5,172-5,313; actual includes 95.8M Power Solutions stub not in the guide (ex-stub +4.0%). Only 2 completed periods found; all beats came in an up-cycle for FTTH, which has now turned.
